hypothesis: Replacing coded edge-to-edge equality with a task-learned comparator operating on independently encoded 16-bit public entity identities can generalize relation transitions to disjoint adversarial aliases and unseen graph families. It is still an engineered representation, and query anchoring plus four-hop traversal remain coded.
train: NEW development-only seeds 41000..41023, graph motifs 0-2, 288 states/576 questions. 120 frozen Adam updates, lr 0.08, max gradient norm 10, weights initialized -1, bias 0, 17 float32 learned scalars. No direct coded equality signal or explicit equality labels; training uses only graph answer labels. Neither future validation query nor true label enters state during inference.
validation: NEW development-only seeds 41200..41211, motifs 4-7, 192 states/384 balanced questions with near-collision aliases generated by frozen F1B algorithm. Independent of W-F2 and all prior Y-F1B/F1C seeds; 576 resident bytes exactly.
arms: One task-trained bit mismatch comparator versus same model before training, frozen sinusoid similarity-only F1B, and fixed coded exact equality upper control. Public ID bits remain programmed features, so this is NOT fully learned identity from raw data.
rubric: DEVELOPMENT_TASK_LEARNED_BIT_COMPARATOR_OBSERVED iff trained validation accuracy>=0.90, false-positive rate<=0.10, and gain >=0.15 against both initialized model and frozen sinusoid similarity. Otherwise DEVELOPMENT_NO_NEW_BIT_COMPARATOR_GENERALIZATION. Either verdict development only; separate sealed first-use required for scientific acceptance.
authority: No accepted source/ref mutation, no queue/controller, no FOREGE R32/R33, no KTRADE, no broker/production, no sealed first use, no paid APIs; archive raw per-question evidence before a final full Yggdrasil regression.
